inputs: direct isolated browser probes and visible form-error screenshots

findings.refutation: The actual visible form contains a clear inline error and an invalid date does not change saved bytes. The brief requires visible feedback without mandating its element or testid. The original oracle excluded all form text and therefore missed this valid behavior. A focused control regression and full rerun corrected the false positive.

Mobile UI visibly says LOCAL EDITION and Saved on this device. Desktop also visibly says Fictional team · Local demo. The initial exact-word regex missed equivalent explicit local-device framing. The app brief describes a fictional local-only demonstration but does not require a fictional-product banner at every viewport. No remote or real shared-team service is represented by these observed controls.

exploratoryFindings.contractAmbiguity: The brief reserves the select value all for the All projects sentinel while allowing any nonempty project string, including all. exploratoryFindings.impact: No collision observed: the distinct project option isolates the intended record, and storage remains unchanged.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop separates a persistent workspace rail from the board. The board title and dark New task button are prominent, followed by a summary, search/filter controls and three clearly named status columns.
observations.implication: The major places and primary action are easy to identify, and the status columns provide a stable organizing structure.

observations.observation: The top introduction, progress summary and spacious filters occupy a substantial band above the task cards. The left rail also devotes space to editorial copy and an illustration. Individual cards have generous padding and a full-width status select.
observations.implication: The layout is calm and readable, but a working user scans relatively few complete cards in the first desktop viewport. Reducing introductory chrome or offering a denser board mode would improve task visibility.

observations.observation: Serif page headings, bold sans-serif task titles, pale neutral/green surfaces and thin borders recur across the board and form. The restrained rust accent appears in progress, priority and visible focus treatment; priority also has a word and directional icon.
observations.implication: The application presents a consistent identity and makes task titles more prominent than metadata without relying only on color for priority.

observations.observation: The modal has distinct labels, required/optional markers, supporting constraints, grouped status/priority fields and clearly separated Cancel/Create actions. The currently focused title field has a conspicuous outline.
observations.implication: The captured form tells users what each field expects and where the keyboard focus is. The screenshot does not establish complete keyboard or screen-reader conformance.

observations.observation: The filtered board shows one matching card, an explicit matching count, a Clear filters control and readable empty states in the other columns. The malformed-import notice names invalid JSON and states that the existing board has not changed.
observations.implication: The captured feedback explains both the current filtered view and the failed import. The capture receipt separately confirms unchanged stored bytes for this one malformed input; it is not a claim about all import cases.

observations.observation: At the captured mobile first visit, the brand/header, large board title, introduction, New task button and expanded progress overview take nearly the entire viewport. Search appears near the bottom, and no task card is visible. The visible elements fit the width without obvious overlap.
observations.implication: The mobile opening favors presentation over immediate access to existing work. Collapsing or shortening the introductory overview would bring the task board into view sooner.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score. Task cards are below the first mobile viewport.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static screenshots cannot establish all keyboard behavior, screen-reader output, motion quality, data safety or import correctness. Those need the separate behavioral rubric.
The board counts and progress percentages belong to this fictional seeded application, not benchmark performance or product adoption.
Anchored screenshots can begin partway through surrounding content because they preserve a real viewport. This is not evidence of source-page clipping.
No condition mapping was inspected, no candidate code was changed and no numerical aesthetic score or causal improvement claim is assigned.

processReview.summary: The Fabius app run read its design reference, expanded failure checks and iterated through focus, contrast and dialog-test failures before successful retests.

observations.observed: The public plan separated board construction, guarded storage behavior, task workflows and mobile/desktop verification.
The pinned design-system reference was read. After the first workflow suite passed, explicit source edits covered imported enum types, a project named all, tag preservation and open-form conflicts.

Edge checks failed on modal focus, then contrast. The run edited focus handling, calculated the color ratios and adjusted a color token. Dialog/protocol and workflow failures also appeared before later successful edge and main-suite runs.
The final documentation was updated from retained result files and reports Chrome-only coverage and storage limitations.

limits: The supplied process did not prevent initial focus and contrast defects.
Some checks overlapped in time and dialog errors occurred; the trace alone cannot assign every failure to product code versus test interactions.
The successful final self-tests remain separate from independent acceptance evaluation.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
